title: Attention kernel fallback + locality synthesis - arch jam notes
content:
Context:
Quick sync after prototype runs for attention-kernel fallback + request-locality-aware slab placement. Aim: decide whether to fold the fallback logic into the runtime kernel selector or keep it as a routing layer policy. Also discuss KV reconciliation impacts when requests are migrated between slots for locality.

Attendees:
- Priya Desai (note taker, infra lead)
- Marcus Chen (kernel team)
- Olivia Park (serving runtime / telemetry)
- Diego Alvarez (SRE)
- Aisha Khan (applied-ml focusing on long-context models)

Goals for session:
- Surface perf numbers from microbench and end-to-end canary
- Choose ownership boundary for fallback behavior (kernel vs routing)
- Outline KV cache reconciliation contract for preempted sessions
- Capture open questions and owners for follow-ups

Summary of prototype runs (Marcus):
- Microbench: fallback path (software attention) vs optimized kernel shows 1.8-2.6x higher CPU on fallback for short sequences (<=128) and 3-4x for long sequences (>=1024) on A100.
- End-to-end (canary) with 200rps synthetic mixed traffic: 95th latency increased from 58ms to 140ms when fallback triggered for 12% of requests.
- Important: fallback often correlates with unexpected input shapes (uneven tokenization) and occasional kernel OOMs at large batch sizes.

Locality placement experiment (Olivia):
- Simple allocator that tries to keep consecutive requests from same tenant in same slab reduced KV-sync events by ~34% in our sim.
- Heatmap shows hot conversation sequences get colocated, but cold-starts still distributed.
- Memory fragmentation increases slightly; need compaction triggers.

Discussion notes / tradeoffs:
1) Ownership of fallback: kernel vs routing
- Marcus: kernel-level fallback keeps decision close to runtime; simpler in terms of correctness (no routing-layer race), but kernel bloat risk and harder to test across hardware families.
- Diego: routing layer fallback enables policy experimentation (SLO-based decisions) and easier metrics, but increases request hop surface and potential for KV cache loss during migration.
- Decision: favor a hybrid approach. Implement a lightweight kernel-level safe-fallback (for immediate, deterministic fallbacks like unsupported op) and expose a routing-layer policy for higher-level SLO-driven fallbacks (e.g., prefer cheaper model variant under load).

2) KV reconciliation contract for slot migration
- Problem: when routing moves a conversation to a different slab/node for locality or load, the KV prefix (KV cache for that session) may be stale or incomplete. Naive full-copy causes latency spikes.
- Proposed contract (Aisha + Olivia):
  - Each KV block stamped with a monotonic sequence + last-updated TTL.
  - Migration procedure: optimistic start on new slab using best-effort async fetch of missing KV pages; fallback to blocking copy only if missing pages requested synchronously.
  - Expose metrics: kv-miss-on-migration, kv-blocking-copy-count.
- Tradeoffs: async fetch keeps latency low but risks slight quality regressions for few tokens; blocking copy guarantees fidelity but increases tail latency.
- Decision: adopt optimistic async-first with configurable blocking threshold per-tenant (default conservative for SLO-critical tenants).

3) Locality-aware slab allocator heuristics
- Heuristics considered:
  - Sticky-by-tenant (coarse): keep same tenant sessions together. Pros: simple; cons: poor inter-tenant fairness.
  - Sticky-by-conversation (fine): attempt to colocate sequential requests from same conversation id. Pros: best KV hit-rate; cons: higher fragmentation.
  - Hybrid TTL-based stickiness: conversation sticky while active, then evict to general pool.
- Decision: implement hybrid TTL stickiness (default 30s active window) with tenant-level caps to avoid noisy-tenant hogging.

4) Telemetry & observability requirements (Olivia)
- Must instrument: fallback-reason, fallback-origin (kernel|routing), kv-migration-latency, kv-async-miss-rate, slab-compaction-events, per-tenant fallback-rate.
- Add lightweight tracing hook so persona (prod vs dev) can see per-request path.
- Action: telemetry proto in github PR#214 to be expanded; Olivia to add sampling plan.

Open questions / Risks:
- Kernel footprint growth and test matrix across device families (A100, H100, AMD). Marcus to draft risk matrix by 2024-09-25.
- Edge case: concurrent migration + compaction may cause missing KV pages; need to ensure idempotent retries. Diego + Aisha to prototype safe ack on compaction.
- Security: cross-tenant KV leakage risk if reuse not zeroed; platform-engineering to audit allocator free-paths. Assigned to Nils (cc: platform-engineering).

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Marcus: small RFC documenting hybrid fallback split (kernel safe-fallback API + routing policy hooks). ETA 2024-09-26.
- Olivia: extend PR#214 with telemetry fields, sampling spec, and annotation examples. ETA 2024-09-22.
- Diego + Aisha: prototype optimistic async KV fetch with blocking threshold and run synthetic canary. ETA 2024-10-03.
- Priya: add confluence page LongContext-Perf-Playbook with runbook for fallback incidents. ETA 2024-09-24.
- Platform-engineering (Nils): security audit of slab free-paths and zeroing strategy. ETA 2024-10-01.

Notes-to-self / rough ideas (brainstorm fragments):
- Could keep small sticky cache of last-N KV pages on routing layer to further reduce blocking copies (cheap to keep).
- Consider per-tenant QoS token-bucket so heavy tenants can be throttled from triggering fallback storms.
- Explore kernel-level guardrails that detect imminent OOM and fail fast to routing fallback to prevent partial kernel corruption.

Meeting follow-up plan:
- Short 30m follow-up next Tuesday to walk through Marcus RFC and Olivia telemetry PR. Schedule invite: 2024-09-24 10:00 PT.

Appendix: quick perf table (from Marcus runs, trimmed)
- Optimized kernel (A100): median 18ms (seq=256), p95 58ms
- Software fallback (A100, same batch): median 42ms, p95 120-160ms depending on long tokens
- Migration copy cost (blocking): +80-200ms depending on KV size

End notes: keep design conservative for default tenants but unlock aggressive async behavior for trusted enterprise tenants via per-tenant config flags (matching Dedicated/Private needs). Priya to track adoption plan in product sync.
